description: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of “Pass@1” scores across different percentage bins, likely representing the performance of a 1B parameter language model under test-time scaling, as referenced in the paper “Can 1B LLM Surpass 405B LLM? Rethinking Compute-Optimal Test-Time Scaling.” The horizontal axis, labeled “Pass@1,” is divided into five bins: [0.0, 0.2), [0.2, 0.4), [0.4, 0.6), [0.6, 0.8), and [0.8, 1.0], indicating the range of success rates for individual test-time samples. The vertical axis, labeled “Percentage,” shows the proportion of samples falling into each bin, scaled from 0.0 to 0.8 in increments of 0.1. The chart features five light blue bars, each annotated with its percentage value: 11.2% in the [0.0, 0.2) bin, 3.4% in [0.2, 0.4), 3.4% in [0.4, 0.6), 5.8% in [0.6, 0.8), and a dominant 76.2% in the [0.8, 1.0] bin. A red dashed vertical line at approximately 0.82 is labeled “mean: 0.82,” indicating the average Pass@1 score across all samples. The chart visually emphasizes the heavy right-skew of performance, with the vast majority of samples achieving high success rates (≥0.8), while very few fall into the lower bins. A small gray square in the legend appears to be a placeholder or unlinked to any visual element in the chart.
